transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on one thing. Like at work, I’ll be fixing some rendering bug, and then a Slack message or even a color on the screen, or a siren outside, just pulls me off into some other idea before I finish what I was doing. It’s… been hard to function.
Did you have this same kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?

Not really like this, no. I mean, I could get distracted sometimes, like any kid, but what’s happening now feels different. I’ll be in the middle of code and one little thing—a Slack ping, or even a color on the screen—just pulls me completely somewhere else before I finish.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or wired, far more than your normal self?

Yeah… there have been times like that. I’ll wake up already sort of… charged, I guess. My head’s immediately on features, code changes, even bigger-picture stuff like layouts or how something should be presented. Sitting still feels almost like I’m wasting time.
During those charged-up times, do you need less sleep than usual?
I’m not totally sure. I mean… I don’t really track it closely. Sometimes I stay up later, but I don’t know if I’d say I need less sleep.
During those charged-up times, do you feel more confident or important than usual?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t usually say it out loud, but in those moments I feel like I’m the only one who can really connect the generative art stuff with Mexican visual traditions and the tech scene here… like it could actually change how the city sees public art.
During those charged-up times, do you take on a lot more projects or work than you usually would?

Yeah… probably. I’ll start a lot of things at once. Like emailing curators, pitching people in the community, reworking the backend, sketching out installation ideas… trying to get other developers involved, even late. It starts feeling bigger than my actual job, I guess.
When you’re in those charged-up periods, do you talk more than usual?

Yeah… I think so. When I get going about the platform, I can kind of just… keep talking. The architecture, funding, what it could mean culturally, how to deploy it—all of it. People have told me it’s hard to jump in, but to me it feels like the ideas are coming too fast to stop.
During those charged-up times, do you feel unusually euphoric or high?

Yeah… kind of. Most days in that state I feel really lit up, like everything I’ve been building finally makes sense and Glendale is… catching up to it. It feels good. Big.

But if people slow me down with “process” or whatever, I can get pretty sharp. My wife, coworkers… I snap more than I should.
During those charged-up periods, do you get much more done than usual or become much more driven to work on projects?

Yeah. I mean… I do get a lot more driven. I’ll be emailing curators, pitching community people, rewriting parts of the backend, sketching installation plans… trying to pull other developers in at odd hours.

It starts to feel like the project is bigger than my regular job, so I just keep pushing on it.
How long do those charged-up periods usually last?
Um… it’s been a while. Maybe about three months now, since the Glendale showcase picked my platform. Since then it’s kind of stayed… charged up.
During this charged-up period, has it caused serious problems at work or at home?

Yeah… it has. Work got pretty bad. My employer put me on leave after I pushed some changes through without waiting for approval.

And at home… my wife says the spending and the arguments are making things feel unstable. I don’t really like putting it that way, but… yeah.
During this charged-up period, have you had experiences like hearing or seeing things that other people couldn’t, or strongly believing something that others said wasn’t true?

I haven’t really seen or heard things, no.

But… I do feel pretty sure there are people circling the platform. Like major museums, maybe a couple investors. The showcase wording, their Instagram posts, even some emails at work… they line up too perfectly. Other people tell me I’m reading into it, but it doesn’t feel random to me.
Do you believe for certain that major museums or investors are secretly signaling about your platform?
Yeah… I mean, I know how it sounds. But yes, I’m pretty sure. The showcase language, the museum posts, even a few work emails… they line up too neatly. It doesn’t feel like coincidence.
